records.name: Sports Complex Special Services District
records.summary: The special services district that looks after streets, trees, and green space around the sports complex in South Philadelphia. Its programs cover litter and leaf pickup, street trees, and dog waste stations for people who live inside the district.
records.what_you_do: Residents can sign up for phone alerts, ask for a new street tree, and come to community events. The district also follows zoning and development plans in the area and shares news about projects such as a new arena and a traffic plan.

schedule.text: Holds an annual board meeting and publishes a yearly report. Other meeting times are not posted on the site.

cost.text: Phone alerts, community events, the recycling cart, and reusable grocery bags are free, according to the programs page.

first_step.how: Call 215-271-1701 and ask to be added to the Autocall phone alert list. Only people who live in the district can join.
first_step.basis: Most programs and the phone alerts are for district residents, and the site does not say how someone from outside the district can take part. The way in is unclear beyond that.
first_step.what_to_expect: The district's work happens on the street: litter pickup, tree care, and dog waste stations. The website does not describe a regular meeting or what one is like, so a phone call to the office is the best first step. The phone alerts, events, and recycling cart cost nothing.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at 215-271-1701 before you go, since no regular meeting times are posted.
Have your home address ready, because the phone alerts and community events are for district residents.
On event days, follow the overhead signs to the event parking lots.

records.notes: Tier 2. records.name: Tasker-Morris Neighbors Association
records.summary: Tasker-Morris Neighbors Association is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the South part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come together to review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers.

first_step.how: Email the contact on the City's list of registered community organizations to ask when the group next meets about nearby zoning and building plans.

records.notes: Tier 2 found no web presence beyond the group's Facebook page. Facebook is a leads-only source, so it was not fetched and no facts were taken from it. Nothing here is newer than tier 1: last_sign_of_life 2026-10 is the City registry listing, not a dated post. The first step points to the registry contact as published. A reviewer should confirm the group still meets before relying on it for a first visit.

records.name: Whitman Council, Inc.
records.summary: A neighborhood advisory council for the Whitman area of South Philadelphia, serving the community since 1977. Its office helps neighbors with utility bills, property tax and rent rebates, senior programs, and other housing questions.
records.what_you_do: Staff help residents apply for utility assistance, property tax and rent rebates, and the senior property tax freeze, and answer questions about SEPTA schedules and zoning. The council also lists its board meetings and community events on its calendar.

schedule.text: Board meetings are listed for Wednesday evenings around 6:30 pm. The site does not say how often they meet.

first_step.how: Call (215) 468-4056 or email whitmancouncilinc@gmail.com to book an appointment at the office on S 3rd Street.
first_step.basis: The site says the council helps anyone who asks, and it gives office hours and a phone number to book a visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Visits are usually booked ahead, since the office prefers appointments. Staff can help with utility assistance, property tax and rent rebates, and LIHEAP or PACE applications. The site does not list costs for these services.
first_visit_tips: Call during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm, to book a time.
Ask about parking and transit when you book, since the site gives no directions for either.
The office is on S 3rd Street at the same address listed for the 2025 board meetings.

records.notes: Tier 2. Office hours, phone, and email come from the contact page. The group's own email (whitmancouncilinc@gmail.com) now sits in contacts.email in place of the City registry address mkapkkz@msn.com; the registry address was not disproved and a reviewer can restore it. Newest dated item is a news post dated March 21, 2026, so last_sign_of_life moved to 2026-03. The calendar runs from 2018 to October 2025 and does not say whether meetings are open to the public. Housing help added as an interest from the About page list of services. Accessibility, dues, and parking are not stated.

records.name: Community Schools @Add B. Anderson
records.summary: Add B. Anderson is one of the City's Community Schools, where volunteers help with after school and family programs. Open shifts are listed on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help with school programs for students and families, such as weekly reading coaching and grocery distribution, per the City's volunteer listing.

schedule.text: Some volunteer roles repeat weekly, such as reading coaching and grocery distribution, per the City's volunteer listing. Days and times are not given.

first_step.how: Call or email the Community School Coordinator, Lyndell Mason, at (267) 226-5850 or lyndell.mason@phila.gov, and ask about the open volunteer roles.
first_step.basis: The City's school page names a coordinator to contact, and the volunteer listing is open to the public. Whether clearances apply to this school was not confirmed this run.
first_step.what_to_expect: The coordinator's listed office hours are weekdays, 8:30 am to 5 pm, so that is the best time to call. The school's programs include after school learning, family events, and student support. The site does not say how long a shift runs, so ask the coordinator.
first_visit_tips: Call the coordinator on a weekday between 8:30 am and 5 pm, when the listed office hours run.
Ask what paperwork or clearances come before a first shift, since the City page does not list them.

records.notes: Tier 2. The City volunteer portal returned HTTP 403 for this school, so it was not read. Volunteer roles and weekly shifts are carried from the tier 1 read of the portal and were not re-checked. The City school page names the coordinator, office hours, and program areas, and says there are no upcoming events, but gives no volunteer steps or clearance list. Contacts now point to the coordinator from the City page. The portal contact Madeline.Cerulli@phila.gov and (215) 834-6277 is kept here for reference. One WebSearch was used to find the City page.

records.name: Community Schools @Alain Locke School
records.summary: Alain Locke School is one of the City's Community Schools, where volunteers help with after school and family programs. Open shifts are listed on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help lead weekly student clubs for grades K to 8 and support school events, per the City's volunteer listing.

schedule.text: Student clubs run weekly, and volunteers are asked to lead one, per the City's volunteer listing. Days and times are not given.

first_step.how: Call Jared Beck, the Community School Coordinator, at (215) 400-7670 or email jared.beck@phila.gov to ask about the club volunteer roles.
first_step.basis: The volunteer listing says school volunteers must clear background and child abuse checks and sign district forms before starting, so the way in takes approval rather than a drop-in visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: The coordinator's listed office hours are weekdays, 8:30 am to 5 pm. Before a first shift, volunteers who work with students need background and child abuse clearances, per the volunteer listing. The school's programs include after school learning, family events, and student support, so ask which club or event you would help with.
first_visit_tips: Call during the coordinator's weekday office hours, 8:30 am to 5 pm.
Ask which clearances apply before you plan a first shift, since the City page does not list them.

records.notes: Tier 2. The City volunteer portal returned HTTP 403 for this school, so club roles and clearance requirements are carried from tier 1 and not re-checked. The City school page gives 4550 Haverford Ave with ZIP 19139, while tier 1 had 19104; the tier 1 ZIP is kept until a reviewer decides. Contacts now point to the coordinator on the City page. The portal contact Madeline.Cerulli@phila.gov and (215) 834-6277 is kept here for reference. The City page says there are no upcoming events and does not list volunteer requirements.

records.name: Drexel Area Property Association
records.summary: A registered community organization for University City property owners, formed in 2012. It keeps members up to date on nearby development projects, and the City asks developers to talk with it about nearby zoning and building plans.
records.what_you_do: Property owners follow development projects in University City and share their views on zoning and building plans. The group also works with community leaders, city officials, and police on safety and neighborhood concerns.

schedule.text: Meets about four times a year, roughly every three months. The site does not give meeting times or a meeting place.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: 3070 Spring Garden St, Suite 2, Philadelphia, PA 19104

first_step.how: Send a message through the Email Us contact at daparco.org/contact and ask about the next meeting.
first_step.basis: The site says the group represents property owners and lists meeting dates, but it does not say who may attend or how to join, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group lists its meetings on its home page, about four times a year. The site does not say how long a meeting runs, who attends, or what it costs, so ask before you come. The office keeps Monday to Saturday hours, 9 am to 5 pm.
first_visit_tips: Send a message before you go, since the site gives no meeting times or place.
The office is at 3070 Spring Garden St, Suite 2, open Monday to Saturday, 9 am to 5 pm.

records.notes: Tier 2. The site calls the group DAPA (A University City Property Association). The City registry name is kept here and a reviewer can choose the name. Membership, attendance, and dues are not stated, so open_to stays public from tier 1 and is not confirmed by the site. The group describes itself as formed by property owners and developers, which is close to the out of scope line for homeowner associations, so a reviewer should check it against the scope rules. 2025 meeting dates were Jan 21, Apr 15, Jul 15, and Oct 21. The office and meeting entries are merged into one because the site names no meeting place.
